title: Modular Assistant Kit — Primer & rough PRD
content:
Context / one-liner:
A lightweight, opinionated kit (JS + REST + example UI) to let teams embed small assistant "modules" (microflows) into apps quickly — minimal infra, optional telemetry, local statelets for session continuity. Focus: fast time-to-value for product teams who want a preview assistant UX without owning full infra.

Why now:
- Customer signals: product teams ask for small assistant pieces (search helper, inline summarizer, email composer) but they don’t want to maintain a whole LLM stack.
- We can bundle serving + client SDK + simple UI patterns + safe defaults (quota, cost SLOs) and position for PLG growth.

Core idea / components (rough):
- microflow: single-purpose assistant (e.g., summarizer) with a manifest (input schema, tokens budget, fallback model list).
- statelet: tiny local session store (keyed by user/id) that persists recent prompts, user preferences, short recaps. Not a full session server.
- adapter: thin client-side library (npm + CDN) for web apps + a tiny server adapter for backend apps. Handles auth, sampling defaults, telemetry toggles.
- template UIs: 3 minimal kit UIs (inline box, slide-over helper, compact composer) implemented in vanilla JS/React examples.
- examples + recipes: snippet library showing typical wiring (search assistant, customer support triage, compose assistant).

Target users / personas:
- PMs at early-stage SaaS wanting to ship an assistant feature in 1–2 sprints.
- Platform/infra-lite teams in mid-market who want prototype UX before committing to Dedicated.
- Developer advocates / solution engineers for quick demos.

Top-level goals (metrics):
- Time-to-prototype: < 3 days from npm install to working demo (goal).
- Activation: % of trial accounts that embed a kit demo (measure via example app + GA).
- Conversion: track kit usage correlated to Dedicated interest (lead signal).
- Cost safety: default token cap + auto-fallback to cheaper model after X tokens.

User stories (examples):
- As a PM, I can drop an inline summarizer component into the product with <20 lines of markup and a server key so I can validate the feature with users.
- As an engineer, I can switch the microflow to a local dev mode that routes to a small local runtime (or mocked responses) for testing.
- As a product manager, I can set a global token budget per user and get alerts when the kit exceeds predicted cost thresholds.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Microflow manifest spec documented (input schema, output schema, models, budget fields).
- NPM package published with adapter + typed client (TS) + README.
- 3 example microflows implemented (summarizer, rewrite/composer, search-responder).
- Example UI for each microflow (React sandbox link) + embed instructions.
- Default telemetry opt-in flag, with clear doc on what is collected.
- Fallback policy implemented: when token budget exceeded -> deterministic fallback to smaller model or canned response.

API sketch (very rough):
- POST /kits/v1/microflows/:id/run
  - body: {user_id, input, state_delta?, client_metadata?}
  - headers: Authorization: Bearer <kit-key>
  - response: {output, tokens_used, model_version, suggested_next_actions?}
- GET /kits/v1/microflows/:id/manifest -> manifest JSON
- POST /kits/v1/statelets/:user_id/patch -> apply small delta to local statelet

Privacy / security notes:
- Default telemetry minimal: counts (tokens, error rates, latency buckets), no PII. Make opt-in explicit in kit install flow.
- Kit keys are scoped to microflows and have rate limits; recommend server-side proxied keys for production.
- Provide a rapid on-prem/local runtime dev path (docker image + single binary) for enterprise evaluation.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Week 0–2: internal hackdays + 1–2 SE demos; collect initial feedback.
- Week 3–5: publish alpha NPM + example repo, invite 5 customer beta teams.
- Week 6–10: iterate on manifest, telemetry toggles, add 2 more microflows, refine docs.
- Post-alpha: measure activation -> determine conversion funnel integration with Dedicated sales.

Open questions / risks (quick):
- Scope creep: teams want full session persistence, but kit aims to remain lightweight. Where do we draw line?
- Pricing model: include kit as free/onboarding? Or tie to token usage and treat as feature of Hosted? (needs GTM discussion)
- Telemetry opt-in friction vs product insights: how to balance?
- Supporting UI frameworks: React + plain JS shipped first; do we build Vue/Svelte examples later?

Implementation TODOs (short backlog):
- [ ] Draft microflow manifest schema (Rae) PROJ-874
- [ ] Minimal adapter + auth flow (Victor) GH PR link in artifacts
- [ ] Build summarizer + composer examples (Sam)
- [ ] Simple fallback engine (runtime-configurable)
- [ ] Docs: quickstart, security, telemetry checklist
- [ ] Internal demo + checklist for SEs

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could provide a "kit playground" page on console where teams can preview components and generate starter code (copy/paste).
- Consider a one-click deploy: embed snippet + console button to create scoped kit-key (like secrets manager) and sample app.
- Low-lift monetization: show usage summary in console, but keep initial friction low (free during alpha).

Links / references:
- Quick sketch repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/assistant-kits (alpha branch)
- Related ticket: PROJ-874 (manifest & admin UI)

Immediate next steps:
- Sync with Rae + Victor tomorrow 10am PT.
- Draft manifest v0.1 by EOD Friday.
- Set up alpha demo instance and get SEs to try embedding in a sandbox product.

Random scribbles:
- "statelet" size cap: 2KB serialized? start small and increase if customers ask.
- Built-in cost preview: estimator in README showing expected token spend for sample inputs.

End of brief.
